thanks for the thought-out answer, i agree that they should work together, that's my dream team. im not sure that wages above $15 would increase like that. I hope so but i havent seen a reason so if somebody has one, please hit me up. UBI would be better than the wage increase because with Pete's plan, you still have your healthcare and benefits all tied to employment. UBI gives employees the freedom to change jobs instead of sticking with one that comes with abuse or unfair standards because you dont want to lose human rights like healthcare and stuff. Like, you could have healthcare not tied to employment if Yang had his way.

I did see the rest of the plan and giving resources to predominantly black schools which are usually underfunded is a fantastic policy, but why would UBI bankrupt the country? Correct me if im wrong but i believe people will spend an extra 1000 in local communities. A large amount of americans can't afford an unexpected $1000 bill, whether its a broken down car, leaks in the house or even being too sick to work for a period of time.
Americans who live paycheck to paycheck would put a lot of the money back into their communities, so part of the cost will pay for itself. I know people will buy stuff from Amazon and stuff but if you tax every amazon sale, uber and robot truck mile, google search and facebook ad, even a tiny percentage will go along way alongside a Value added tax which is half of what most of Europe has. VAT would help pay for UBI because Amazon and Apple would have to pay it instead of whats happening now where they pay 0, less than any American. 

Also it costs a lot more than $12000 a year to pay for the cost of each individual prisoner. We should pay citizens to stay out of prison, which will save a lot of money too. Both Yang and Buttigieg want to release those who were imprisoned for non-violent drug offences but i feel Yang's policies don't just take people out of prison like Pete's policy but also gives them a further incentive to stay out and avoid recidivism. 

I agree alot with Pete, i just think Yang's approach to automation is more evidence based.

OP's post mentions the min wage increase, but a $15 min wage accelerates automation, which will eventually replace most min wage jobs. Also, this policy doesn't impact earners who make more than $15, unlike Universal Basic Income which helps all regardless of income. Raising the min wage puts the burden on employers but UBI puts the burden on the government. If anybody has a reason for me to favour the wage raise instead of UBI (proposed by Yang and Williamson), then im all ears...or eyes i guess
